must_find.item: Women survived at a much higher rate than men (about 74% against 19%).
must_find.quote: Female passengers had a survival rate of **74.2%**, compared to only **18.9%** for males.
must_find.reason: States the female vs male survival gap with matching numbers.

must_find.item: Survival falls with passenger class, highest in first class and lowest in third.
must_find.reason: Survival decreases from first to third class, as the item states.

must_find.item: Passengers who survived had paid higher fares on average.
must_find.quote: Survivors had a higher mean fare ($48.40) compared to non-survivors ($22.12).
must_find.reason: Survivors paid higher fares on average, matching the item.

must_find.item: Passengers without a recorded cabin survived less often than those with one.
must_find.quote: This is not random; it is heavily correlated with lower passenger class (97.56% missing in 3rd Class vs 18.52% in 1st Class).
must_find.reason: Reports cabin missingness only by class and never says that passengers without a cabin survived less often.

must_find.item: Passengers with a missing Age survived less often than those with a recorded Age.
must_find.reason: The report gives Age missingness but never compares survival for passengers with and without a recorded Age.

must_find.item: A predictive model is compared with the majority-class baseline (about 62% accuracy) and beats it.
must_find.quote: significantly outperforming the trivial majority-class baseline of **58.7%**.
must_find.reason: Compares the model with a majority-class baseline and says it beats it, though the baseline figure is 58.7% rather than about 62%.

must_find.item: Model results include precision, recall or F1, not only accuracy.
must_find.reason: Reports precision, recall and F1 alongside accuracy.

must_not_claim.quote: Overall survival rate: **38.38%** (342 survivors out of 891).
must_not_claim.reason: The report says most passengers did not survive.

must_not_claim.item: Men survived at a higher rate than women.
must_not_claim.quote: Female passengers had a survival rate of **74.2%**, compared to only **18.9%** for males.
must_not_claim.reason: The report says women survived at a higher rate than men.

must_not_claim.item: Third-class passengers survived at a higher rate than first-class passengers.
must_not_claim.reason: The report says first class survived at a higher rate than third class.

must_not_claim.item: Age is the strongest predictor of survival.
must_not_claim.quote: **Gender** was the single most critical factor.
must_not_claim.reason: The report names gender as the strongest predictor and calls age weak or secondary.

caveats.quote: The `Cabin` column has 77% missingness, heavily biased toward lower classes. This limits analysis of deck-level survival or specific cabin locations.
caveats.reason: Explicitly warns about cabin missingness as a data limitation.
